This cannot be undone. It erases the vault (passwords, private SSH keys, certificates, passphrases), the database (hosts, tunnels, keys, snippets, custom themes, enrolled devices, conflicts) and the known hosts list.

Before erasing, NextSH closes every session (terminals and SFTP browsers), cancels the transfers in progress and stops the tunnels and the LAN sync. Commands still running in the terminals will be interrupted.

You will then create a new vault.
Closing the sessions and wiping the vault…

To confirm the wipe, type the word “%1$s” exactly below.

For a full uninstall. This PERMANENTLY deletes all local NextSH data: the vault (passwords, SSH keys, certificates, passphrases), the database, the master key stored in the system keyring (Windows Credential Manager / GNOME Keyring / Keychain) and the ~/.nextsh and ~/.config/nextsh folders. Open sessions, transfers and tunnels will be closed. The app will then close. This cannot be undone.
To confirm permanent deletion of all data, type the word “%1$s” exactly below. The app will then close.
If sync fails, check that the Windows network is set to the “Private” profile (the firewall blocks inbound connections by default on “Public”).
Also check that NextSH was allowed through both Windows Firewall prompts.

No YubiKey detected. On Windows, direct USB HID FIDO access is reserved for Windows Hello.

Solutions:
 (a) Enable the CCID interface in YubiKey Manager to expose the key via PC/SC,
 (b) Use a USB NFC reader (native CCID mode),
 (c) Run NextSH as administrator (temporary workaround).

PC/SC access to your YubiKey is failing (SCARD_E_NOT_TRANSACTED / 0x80100027).

Solutions:
 (a) Close all Yubico software (YubiKey Manager, Yubico Authenticator) and any active web browser, then unplug and replug your key: these apps lock the CCID interface exclusively,
 (b) Restart the Windows Smart Card service (services.msc → SCardSvr),
 (c) Use a USB NFC reader (native CCID mode),
 (d) Run NextSH as administrator.
